title: Cancel serves two callers: an operator stop and a teardown revoke, and only one wants a cancellation record
description:
From the qeu final review (gcx), wave 11 review pass. Introduced by wave 11.

o3n made Cancel's hasSettled ask the operating system before trusting a report,
which is right for the case it was written for: an operator stopping a worker
that wrote its report and kept running. Before the fix that cancel revoked the
credential, killed the process tree, wrote NO durable refusal, and acknowledged
that no stop was requested.

But Cancel has two callers that want different things, and the fix only
considered one:

- The OPERATOR stop. Something is still spending and a person wants it stopped.
  A live process means the attempt has not settled, and a durable cancel.json is
  exactly the record that should exist.
- The TEARDOWN (dispatch.go tearDown, reached from cleanUp AFTER a successful
  collect, gate and close). Cancel is called only to keep A1's order — revoke
  before dispose. Here the attempt SUCCEEDED. If its runner happens to still be
  alive in the narrow window after the report is written (the shape the
  `report_then_addall` fixture exists for: report first, then commit), the
  liveness check now calls it unsettled and writes cancel.json over an attempt
  that finished. inspect reads cancel.json first, so a successfully closed
  attempt afterwards reads as `cancelled`.

The impact today is small — cleanUp is the last thing a run does and the tick is
already closed — but the record is false, and this codebase's whole argument is
that its durable records are true.

What to decide: whether Cancel should take the caller's intent (a stop versus a
teardown-revoke), or whether the executor should distinguish "settled itself"
from "has nothing left to stop" as two separate questions, or whether tearDown
should call a revoke-only operation instead of Cancel. The third is probably
cleanest — tearDown does not want a cancellation, it wants A1's order — but it
adds an executor operation, so it is a contract question rather than a patch.
acceptance_criteria: A successful attempt whose runner is still alive when cleanUp runs is NOT recorded as cancelled, and still has its credential revoked before dispose; an operator cancelling a live worker still gets a durable cancel.json and StopRequested true; a test covers both callers against the same live-after-report fixture.
